headline.label: Company-wide item return rate, Oct 2025 to Sep 2026
headline.context: Returned items as a share of items delivered or returned. Cancelled items left out.

charts.title: Suits & Sport Coats and Socks return most above average
charts.subtitle: Category return rate minus company rate, in points. Oct 2025 to Sep 2026. Categories with 100+ items only.

charts.title: Motherhood Maternity runs 5 points above average
charts.subtitle: Brand return rate minus company rate, in points. Oct 2025 to Sep 2026. Brands with 100+ items only. Top 15 shown.

charts.title: Company return rate has stayed in a 25% to 31% band
charts.subtitle: Monthly item return rate by order month. Aug and Sep 2026 are still maturing, so returns may rise.

charts.title: High-gap categories swing month to month with no clear climb
charts.subtitle: Monthly item return rate by order month for four categories with the biggest gaps. Small monthly volumes make swings noisy.

findings: Across the last 12 months, 28.3% of items delivered or returned were returned (6,437 of 22,785).
Suits & Sport Coats has the highest category gap at 31.4%, which is 3.1 points above average on 663 items. Socks follows at 30.7% (+2.4 points), then Leggings at 30.5% (+2.3 points).
Jeans has the most returned items of any category, at 477, with a rate of 30.3% (+2.0 points). Jeans is the largest category to take to a review.

Motherhood Maternity has the highest brand rate at 33.6% (+5.3 points), followed by 7 For All Mankind at 32.1% and Columbia at 32.1%. These brands have only 140 to 190 items each, so a few returns move the rate.

No category or brand shows a clear month-by-month rise. Monthly rates swing a lot. For example, Socks ran from 21.2% in December 2025 to 45.9% in June 2026, and then fell back to 26.8% in September 2026.

August and September 2026 orders may still see returns come in, so their rates are likely understated. Returns are counted in the month of the order. The data has no return reasons, so it shows where returns are high but not why. Brand is used in place of supplier.
